title: Renewable continuity
blurb: The course's central argument, followed through the five places it does most of its work.

steps.why: States the pattern: order emerges, a threat fractures it, right action restores it, and the work repeats.
Creation is the first instance of the pattern and never a finished event.
The sun performs the same restoration every night.
Kingship and ethics are the human share of the same maintenance.
Death poses the pattern at the scale of a single person.

title: From creation to daily temple service
blurb: How a cosmogony becomes a repeated morning routine performed by named officials.

steps.why: Local traditions describe how differentiated life began.
Explains why several accounts could stand at once without a winner.
The temple models the created world and re-enacts its maintenance daily.
Names the effective power the rite depends on.

title: Re through night and day
blurb: The solar circuit from sunset to sunrise, and the compositions that map it.

steps.why: The cycle in outline, with its forms of the sun.
The royal Underworld Books divide the night into hours and gates.
Locates the Duat among sky, west, water, and tomb without flattening them into one map.

title: Osiris, succession, death, and regeneration
blurb: A family conflict that carries kingship, mourning, and the afterlife.

steps.why: The core relationships and the conflict that drives them.
Set is not a constant villain; his reputation changes across periods.
Funeral ritual applies the Osirian pattern to ordinary dead.
Judgment and vindication complete the sequence for an individual.

title: Maat across ethics, kingship, and ritual
blurb: One word doing work in three registers.

steps.why: Defines the pair and the royal responsibility.
Turns maat into advice about listening, restraint, and speech.
Presenting maat is a physical offering in temple ritual.
The heart is weighed against maat at the threshold.

title: Body, name, ka, ba, and akh
blurb: Why 'soul' is the wrong translation, and what each aspect needed.

steps.why: The whole set and the problems each aspect solves.
Ritual addresses each aspect in a specific way.
Spells for integrity, mobility, and provisioning name these needs directly.

title: Nile, sacred geography, Sobek, and Hapi
blurb: Religion read from the shape of the land and the behaviour of the river.

steps.why: Orientation first: upstream is south, and the west belongs to the dead.
A deity whose range follows water, marsh, and royal patronage.
Takes the same geography to specific standing sites.

title: Pyramid Texts to Coffin Texts to Book of the Dead
blurb: Overlapping corpora, kept overlapping. The ladder model is the thing to unlearn.

steps.why: States why replacement is the wrong model.
The earliest surviving corpus, and the debate about what it was for.
Wider access, new media, continuing material.
Individual commissions that still reuse much older spells.
